source_text:
Fragmentum in epistulam ii ad Thessalonicenses
2 Thess 2,78 Ὅταν μέντοι τὸ πέρας ἐπιστῇ τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ προθεσμίας, καὶ ὁ
νῦν κατέχων αὐτὸν ὅρος ἐκστῇ πληρωθείς, ἑτοίμως τότε καὶ δίχα πάσης ἀναβολῆς ὁ
ἄνομος ἀποκαλυφθήσεται.
thought_title: The lawless one revealed when the appointed time ends
orientation: Gennadius is commenting on 2 Thessalonians 2:7-8, explaining the timing and manner of the lawless one's revelation.
pass_a_gloss: Fragment on the Second Epistle to the Thessalonians. 2 Thess 2,78: But when the end of God's appointed time arrives, and the boundary that now restrains the lawless one, having fulfilled its purpose, is removed, then immediately and without any delay the lawless one will be revealed.

choices.english: the boundary that now restrains him
choices.why: Keeps the present-time force of νῦν and the active restraining sense of κατέχων, while using the glossary English for ὅρος.
rejected: the boundary now holding him back

choices.why: ἐξίστημι here means to withdraw or step aside from a position; πληρωθείς is a passive participle giving the condition or reason for the withdrawal.

choices.term: ἑτοίμως τότε καὶ δίχα πάσης ἀναβολῆς
choices.english: then readily and without any delay
choices.why: ἑτοίμως is an adverb of manner meaning promptly or readily; δίχα πάσης ἀναβολῆς is a prepositional phrase meaning without any postponement, and πάσης strengthens the negation.
rejected: then ready and apart from all delay
then promptly and with no postponement at all

choices.english: the lawless one will be revealed
choices.why: Uses the glossary English for ὁ ἄνομος and the future passive of ἀποκαλύπτω for the public disclosure.
rejected: the lawless one will be disclosed

bible_refs.note: ὁ κατέχων and ὁ ἄνομος ἀποκαλυφθήσεται echo the language of 2 Thess 2:7-8 about the restrainer and the revelation of the lawless one.

pass_b_english: But when the end of God's appointed time arrives, and the boundary that now restrains him steps aside, having been fulfilled, then the lawless one will be revealed readily and without any delay.
notes: The source notation '2 Thess 2,78' appears to be a typographical error or unusual notation, likely intended as 2:7-8 or 2:7,8; reproduced as found.

last_rejected.why: 'Steps aside' implies voluntary movement; ἐκστῇ means 'is removed/withdrawn' (passive/middle sense of standing away).
last_rejected.ruling: ἐκστῇ (from ἐφίστημι/ἐκστήναι) means 'stand away/withdraw'; 'steps aside' is within normal range, not a major error.

problems.quote: what now restrains him
problems.why: Same Greek concept rendered as 'what' then 'boundary'—reader thinks two different things.
problems.fix: Use consistent term: 'restrainer' or 'the one who restrains'.

problems.quote: its task complete
problems.why: Different participles for same Greek; reader may miss parallel.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'having been fulfilled' or 'when his task is complete'.

problems.quote: at once
problems.why: Same Greek adverb (eutheos/etoi) rendered differently; 'readily' is odd here.
problems.fix: Use 'immediately' or 'at once' consistently.

problems.quote: its task complete, steps aside
problems.why: 'Task complete' vs. 'having been fulfilled' suggest different subjects doing the fulfilling.
problems.fix: Pick one phrasing for the restraining force's completion.

problems.why: 'At once' and 'readily' differ in connotation; reader may detect a nuance change.
problems.fix: Use 'at once' consistently or note the variants.
